Which actions can a Migration run, compared with what a trace records?

Long image

A

Answer

A run changes the model only at the jump, with the actions a trace records. Its steps exist for data, which traces never record. The runner enforces this split only in versioned-git, and the rule is written nowhere: that gap is #741.

  1. Traces record four Entity actions and instance writes on the model section, nothing on data.1
  2. Generation uses the records only to check that they give the to model; the Migration it writes lists changes and empty data steps.2
  3. Without Git, the jump rewrites the model to the to snapshot with createEntity, alterEntityAttribute and instance writes, the trace vocabulary.3
  4. Steps accept any action; only versioned-git refuses model writes in them.4

Applies toCode on _integration at 70730b2, after #739, #740 and #742 merged. Authoring and following deployments of one application.

1

How do traces, generation and a run connect?

Diagram structure
  • Model edits authoring
  • Trace records records
  • Version snapshots snapshots
  • generateMigration generate
  • Migration row migration
  • runMigration run
  • Jump to target model jump
  • Data steps steps
  • DeploymentState state
  • authoring → records · traced
  • generate → migration · draft
  • migration → run · copied
  • records → snapshots · freeze or tag
  • run → jump · model
  • run → steps · data
  • snapshots → generate · diff, replay check
  • steps → state · recorded
  1. Model edits ↗

    Each model change made through a commit or a direct write becomes a trace record, if traces are on.

  2. Version snapshots ↗

    A freeze (internal) fixes the model and adds a version marker to the records. A tag (Git) fixes the commit, whose records end there.

  3. generateMigration ↗

    Replays the records from from and refuses if they do not give to. The changes come from the diff of the two snapshots.

  4. Migration row ↗

    Holds the changes (classified), empty fill steps per added attribute, empty contract steps per removed Entity or attribute.

  5. Jump ↗

    Brings the model to the to snapshot: applyModelState or a checkout of the tag. The records are not replayed here.

  6. Steps ↗

    Run the designer's data actions on the following deployment, one at a time, each recorded in DeploymentState.

The records never travel to the following deployment. They only vouch for the draft. The model a run installs is the snapshot, written with the same action types the records hold.5

The four rows marked as gaps let a step change the model outside the jump. Before the jump, the jump overwrites the change. After the jump, the deployment's state says to while its model differs from to. Test C5 even asserts that a nested createEntity in a contract step is stored.6

3

Which actions make sense in a step, then?

Your intuition holds for the model: every model write of a run belongs to the jump, and the jump already uses only trace actions. A step needs other actions because data is what traces leave out.

Kind of actionIn a stepWhy
Instance writes on data (create, update, delete)CoreYesFill new attributes, move values, clean up rows. Same action types as traced, on a section traces skip.
Queries and transformer templatesYesCompute the new values from the rows a step reads.
compositeRunTestAssertion, compositeFailYesStop a run whose data is not as the step expects.
Storage drops for removed Entities and attributesContract only, once #733 existsDrop storage, not model rows: the jump already removed the rows.
Any model write: Entity actions, writes on model or modelVersionDiverges from toNoThe jump owns the model.
resetModel, initModel, freeze, generate, nested runMigrationNoThey rewrite or version the model.
Git actions, undo, redo, store, bundle, external servicesNoOutside what a data step does.
transactionalInstanceActionNo, or unwrap itIts write waits for a commit no step makes.

Open point for the designer

Should a fill step ever need an attribute the to model removed? Narrowing N3 says no: such a step goes to #215.

4

What would #741 then cover?

  1. One rule in both modes

    A step holds only data writes outside model and modelVersion, reads, and assertions. The runner checks this list before the first step, as it does today for Git.

  2. Contract drops

    The empty contract steps wait for the storage-drop action of #733.

  3. Outside a run

    A following versioned-git deployment refuses Git actions that change its model, so only the jump checks a tag out.

  4. Test C5

    It is inverted: a nested createEntity in a step is refused, in both modes.
